Definition: Whether the digital ID is recognized or interoperable across borders through regional agreements or travel documents
Comments: No evidence found of cross-border recognition of Angola's national ID card (BI) as a travel or identity document in regional contexts. Angola is a SADC member state; the SADC protocol on free movement of persons is not yet implemented for Angola. The Botswana-Namibia bilateral agreement (2023) for ID card travel does not include Angola. Angola participates in the KAZA visa agreement (2024) covering the KAZA transfrontier area with Botswana, Namibia, Zambia and Zimbabwe but this relates to visas, not ID card recognition. Angola's biometric passport programme is still under development (contract signed 2023). Searched SADC protocols, KAZA agreement, and Angola bilateral travel agreements.

revised_comments: No authoritative evidence identifies formal cross-border recognition or interoperability of Angola's national identity credential through regional agreements or as a recognised travel document. Angola is a SADC member state, but the 2005 SADC Protocol on the Facilitation of Movement of Persons is not fully implemented for Angola, and bilateral arrangements such as the Namibia-Angola border resident card scheme remain at a planning/pilot stage rather than an operational cross-border ID recognition mechanism.
